hook: Thrun proved autonomous driving was possible by winning DARPA's toughest robotics prize, then built the Google program that turned that proof into Waymo, the industry's leading self-driving company, while separately co-founding Udacity to bring university-grade technical education online.
name: Sebastian Thrun

quote.text: Given how quickly the world is changing, I think it's the most important thing we can do, is help people learn.
quote.context: Widely quoted from Thrun's talks on online education, following the launch of Udacity, 2012

moniker: Founder of Google's Self-Driving Car Project and Udacity

reading.body:
Sebastian Thrun's most consequential contribution to AI is a proof of concept: in 2005, Stanley completed a 132-mile off-road course to win the DARPA Grand Challenge, demonstrating that autonomous navigation was achievable before the industry existed to pursue it.

That proof had a direct institutional afterlife. Thrun founded Google's self-driving car project in 2009, and that project became Waymo. The sequence from academic robotics competition to research lab to operating company is unusually clean, and it shows how a single hardware-and-software demonstration can anchor an entire commercial sector. The data does not speak to compute infrastructure or power requirements at any stage, so no claim about those constraints is warranted here.

The second arc runs parallel. A free online AI course in 2011 drew over 160,000 enrolled students, and Thrun co-founded Udacity the following year to give that experiment a permanent institutional form. These two tracks, building autonomous systems and distributing the knowledge to build them, define what the data covers. What it does not cover is the long-term outcomes of Udacity graduates, the current technical state of Waymo's systems, or Thrun's work after 2012.

Founded and led Google's self-driving car project, which became Waymo
Co-founded Udacity (2012), pioneering the MOOC model alongside Coursera
Former director of the Stanford Artificial Intelligence Laboratory
